subject: maths

concepts.title: Equality of Ordered Pairs
concepts.definition: Two paired entries enclosed in brackets match if and only if their initial components coincide and their subsequent components also coincide.
concepts.formula: (x1, y1) = (x2, y2) iff x1 = x2 and y1 = y2
concepts.key_idea: Equating corresponding coordinates yields solvable individual equations for unknowns.
question_patterns: if two ordered pairs are equal find the values of x and y
calculate unknown parameters from equal ordered coordinate pairs
find x and y when (x/3 + 1, y - 2/3) equals (5/3, 1/3)
determine the variables making two coordinate pairs identical
solve for unknown terms given the equality of two ordered pairs

solution_steps.explain: Set the first component of the left pair equal to the first component of the right pair.
Set the second component of the left pair equal to the second component of the right pair.
Isolate the variables to obtain their respective numerical values.

concepts.title: Number of Elements in Cartesian Product
concepts.definition: The total count of coordinate pairs formed by combining elements from two finite collections is the simple product of their individual cardinalities.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplying the counts of members in two sets gives the size of their Cartesian product.
question_patterns: find the number of elements in the cartesian product A x B
calculate the cardinality of A cross B given n(A) and n(B)
what is the total number of ordered pairs in P x Q
how many elements are in the product set of two finite sets
determine n(A x B) when the sizes of sets A and B are known

solution_steps.explain: The size of the product set is the product of individual set sizes.

concepts.title: Cartesian Product of Sets and Triplets
concepts.definition: The collection containing every possible ordered grouping formed by taking the first member from the first collection and each succeeding member from successive collections.
concepts.formula: A x B = {(a, b) : a in A, b in B}
concepts.key_idea: Systematically pairing every element of the leading set with all entries of following sets.
question_patterns: form the cartesian product P x Q and Q x P
find the cross product of sets A and B
construct the set of ordered triplets A x A x A
verify distributive properties of cartesian products over union and intersection
determine original sets A and B from a given cartesian product list

solution_steps.explain: List all members belonging to each constituent set.
Form ordered pairs or triplets taking members in the designated sequence.

concepts.title: Total Number of Relations Between Finite Sets
concepts.definition: Since any binary linkage between two sets is a subset of their Cartesian product, the total possible linkages equals two raised to the product of their cardinalities.
concepts.key_idea: The count of all possible relations equals the number of subsets of the Cartesian product.
question_patterns: find the number of relations from set A to set B
calculate how many subsets exist in the cartesian product A x B
what is the total count of binary relations between two sets
determine the number of possible relations from A into B
how many different relations can be defined from set P to set Q

solution_steps.explain: Find the total ordered pairs in the product set.
Raise two to the power of pair_count to find total subsets.

concepts.title: Domain, Range, and Codomain of a Relation
concepts.definition: For any binary relation, the domain collects every first coordinate, the range collects every active second coordinate, and the codomain is the entire destination set.
concepts.formula: Domain = {x : (x, y) in R}, Range = {y : (x, y) in R}
concepts.key_idea: Domain consists of active starting inputs, while range contains all output images within the codomain.
question_patterns: write down the domain, codomain and range of relation R
represent a relation using roster form and find its range
determine the domain and range of a relation defined on integers
construct the arrow diagram and list domain and range elements
find the set of images and preimages for a given relation

solution_steps.explain: Generate all valid ordered pairs fulfilling the relational rule.
Gather unique first components to form the domain.
Gather unique second components to form the range.

concepts.title: Function Definition and Verification
concepts.definition: A mapping is a special association wherein every member of the source set associates with exactly one unique outcome in the target set.
concepts.formula: f: A -> B where for all a in A, there exists a unique b in B such that f(a) = b
concepts.key_idea: Every input must possess an output and no single input may branch to multiple distinct outputs.
question_patterns: examine whether each of the following relations is a function or not
state giving reasons if a relation defines a function
check if every element in the domain has a unique image
determine whether a given piecewise rule defines a function
identify if a set of ordered pairs qualifies as a function

solution_steps.explain: Ensure every element of the initial set appears as a first component.
Confirm no first component is paired with more than one distinct second component.

concepts.title: Standard Real Functions and Graphs
concepts.definition: Core foundational real-valued mappings including identity, constant, polynomial, rational, absolute value, signum, and greatest integer functions.
concepts.formula: |x| = x for x >= 0, -x for x < 0; sgn(x) = x/|x| for x != 0; [x] <= x
concepts.key_idea: Standard functional models exhibit distinct characteristic curves, domains, and output ranges.
question_patterns: draw the graph of the modulus function and state its domain and range
define the signum function and determine its range
evaluate values of the greatest integer function [x]
find the domain and range of the reciprocal function 1/x
sketch the graph of polynomial functions like x^2 and x^3

solution_steps.explain: Recognize whether the function is absolute value, signum, floor, or polynomial.
Evaluate outputs according to standard piecewise or algebraic definitions.

concepts.title: Algebra of Real Functions
concepts.definition: Arithmetic operations on real-valued functions defined pointwise across the intersection of their respective domains.
concepts.key_idea: Combine function expressions point by point while excluding points where denominators vanish.
question_patterns: find f + g, f - g, fg and f/g for given real functions
calculate the sum and product of two algebraic functions
evaluate the quotient of two real functions stating the restriction
determine the formula for the scalar multiple of a function
perform pointwise algebraic operations on real functions

solution_steps.explain: Add, subtract, multiply, or divide the function rules algebraically.
Ensure denominator expressions are non-zero for quotient functions.

concepts.title: Domain and Range of Real Functions
concepts.definition: The domain is the set of all real numbers for which an algebraic formula produces real outputs, and the range is the resulting set of actual outputs.
concepts.formula: Domain = {x in R : f(x) in R}, Range = {f(x) : x in Domain}
concepts.key_idea: Exclude values causing division by zero or negative values under even roots.
question_patterns: find the domain and range of the function sqrt(9 - x^2)
calculate the domain of rational function f(x) = P(x)/Q(x)
determine the range of real function f(x) = x^2 + 2
find the domain of f(x) = (x^2 + 2x + 1)/(x^2 - 8x + 12)
what is the domain and range of the function f(x) = sqrt(x - 1)

solution_steps.explain: Formulate inequalities for radicals or non-zero conditions for denominators.
Solve constraints to find permissible real values of x.
Analyze expression bounds to deduce the corresponding range.

worked_examples.question_pattern: If the set A has {n_a} elements and the set B has {n_b} elements, find the number of elements in (A x B).

solution_template.explain: The total elements in A x B is n(A) multiplied by n(B).

worked_examples.question_pattern: If set P has {n_a} elements and set Q has {n_b} elements, compute n(P x Q).

solution_template.explain: The size of the product set is the product of individual set sizes.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Let A have {n_a} elements and B have {n_b} elements. Find the number of relations from A to B.

solution_template.explain: Multiply the number of elements in A and B to find pairs.
Calculate 2 raised to the power of pair_count to find total relations.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Let A = {x, y, z} with {n_a} elements and B = {1, 2} with {n_b} elements. Find the number of relations from A to B.

solution_template.explain: Find the total number of ordered pairs.
Find 2 to the power of pair_count.

questions: 1. If (x/3 + 1, y - 2/3) = (5/3, 1/3), find the values of x and y.
2. If the set A has 3 elements and the set B = {3, 4, 5}, then find the number of elements in (A x B).
3. If G = {7, 8} and H = {5, 4, 2}, find G x H and H x G.

4. State whether each of the following statements are true or false: (i) If P = {m, n} and Q = {n, m}, then P x Q = {(m, n),(n, m)}. (ii) If A and B are non-empty sets, then A x B is a non-empty set of ordered pairs (x, y) such that x in A and y in B. (iii) If A = {1, 2}, B = {3, 4}, then A x (B intersect phi) = phi.
5. If A = {-1, 1}, find A x A x A.
6. If A x B = {(a, x),(a, y), (b, x), (b, y)}, find A and B.
7. Let A = {1, 2}, B = {1, 2, 3, 4}, C = {5, 6} and D = {5, 6, 7, 8}. Verify that (i) A x (B intersect C) = (A x B) intersect (A x C), (ii) A x C is a subset of B x D.
8. Let A = {1, 2} and B = {3, 4}. Write A x B. How many subsets will A x B have? List them.
9. Let A and B be two sets such that n(A) = 3 and n(B) = 2. If (x, 1), (y, 2), (z, 1) are in A x B, find A and B, where x, y and z are distinct elements.
10. The Cartesian product A x A has 9 elements among which are found (-1, 0) and (0, 1). Find the set A and the remaining elements of A x A.
1. Let A = {1, 2, 3,...,14}. Define a relation R from A to A by R = {(x, y) : 3x - y = 0, where x, y in A}. Write down its domain, codomain and range.

2. Define a relation R on the set N of natural numbers by R = {(x, y) : y = x + 5, x is a natural number less than 4; x, y in N}. Depict this relationship using roster form. Write down the domain and the range.
3. A = {1, 2, 3, 5} and B = {4, 6, 9}. Define a relation R from A to B by R = {(x, y): the difference between x and y is odd; x in A, y in B}. Write R in roster form.
4. The Fig 2.7 shows a relationship between the sets P and Q. Write this relation (i) in set-builder form (ii) roster form. What is its domain and range?
5. Let A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}. Let R be the relation on A defined by {(a, b): a, b in A, b is exactly divisible by a}. (i) Write R in roster form (ii) Find the domain of R (iii) Find the range of R.
6. Determine the domain and range of the relation R defined by R = {(x, x + 5) : x in {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}}.
7. Write the relation R = {(x, x^3) : x is a prime number less than 10} in roster form.
8. Let A = {x, y, z} and B = {1, 2}. Find the number of relations from A to B.
9. Let R be the relation on Z defined by R = {(a, b): a, b in Z, a - b is an integer}. Find the domain and range of R.

1. Which of the following relations are functions? Give reasons. If it is a function, determine its domain and range: (i) {(2,1), (5,1), (8,1), (11,1), (14,1), (17,1)}, (ii) {(2,1), (4,2), (6,3), (8,4), (10,5), (12,6), (14,7)}, (iii) {(1,3), (1,5), (2,5)}.
2. Find the domain and range of the following real functions: (i) f(x) = -|x|, (ii) f(x) = sqrt(9 - x^2).
3. A function f is defined by f(x) = 2x - 5. Write down the values of (i) f(0), (ii) f(7), (iii) f(-3).

4. The function t which maps temperature in degree Celsius into temperature in degree Fahrenheit is defined by t(C) = 9C/5 + 32. Find (i) t(0), (ii) t(28), (iii) t(-10), (iv) The value of C, when t(C) = 212.
5. Find the range of each of the following functions: (i) f(x) = 2 - 3x, x in R, x > 0, (ii) f(x) = x^2 + 2, x is a real number, (iii) f(x) = x, x is a real number.

1. The relation f is defined by f(x) = x^2 for 0 <= x <= 3 and 3x for 3 <= x <= 10. The relation g is defined by g(x) = x^2 for 0 <= x <= 2 and 3x for 2 <= x <= 10. Show that f is a function and g is not a function.
3. Find the domain of the function f(x) = (x^2 + 2x + 1)/(x^2 - 8x + 12).
4. Find the domain and the range of the real function f defined by f(x) = sqrt(x - 1).
5. Find the domain and the range of the real function f defined by f(x) = |x - 1|.
6. Let f = {(x, x^2/(1 + x^2)) : x in R} be a function from R into R. Determine the range of f.
7. Let f, g : R -> R be defined by f(x) = x + 1, g(x) = 2x - 3. Find f + g, f - g and f/g.
8. Let f = {(1,1), (2,3), (0,-1), (-1,-3)} be a function from Z to Z defined by f(x) = ax + b, for some integers a, b. Determine a, b.

9. Let R be a relation on N defined by R = {(a, b) : a, b in N and a = b^2}. Are the following true? (i) (a, a) in R for all a in N, (ii) (a, b) in R implies (b, a) in R, (iii) (a, b) in R, (b, c) in R implies (a, c) in R.
10. Let A = {1, 2, 3, 4}, B = {1, 5, 9, 11, 15, 16} and f = {(1, 5), (2, 9), (3, 1), (4, 5), (2, 11)}. Are the following true? (i) f is a relation from A to B, (ii) f is a function from A to B.
11. Let f be the subset of Z x Z defined by f = {(ab, a + b) : a, b in Z}. Is f a function from Z to Z? Justify your answer.
12. Let A = {9, 10, 11, 12, 13} and let f : A -> N be defined by f(n) = the highest prime factor of n. Find the range of f.
